reasons: Both answers make the same core argument well: habituation, the tickets are really about recovery, and a tiered approach with undo, trash and type-to-confirm only for boards. Neither names the downstream effects of the friction such as users avoiding deletes, stale boards or archiving workarounds; A comes closest by predicting that friction tickets will replace lost-data tickets. B wins on a more complete, spec-ready edge-case list (subtasks, restoring into a trashed board, IME composition, clicking outside the modal, Backspace-triggered deletes, trash permissions, purge and audit) and a wireframe, while A's best extra is the idea of typing the count for bulk deletes.
